title: A Little Tune for Thunder
story: I Will Trust and Not Be Afraid
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The thunder walked across the roof,
The window rattled loud;
I put my hand upon my heart
And hummed beneath the cloud.

[Chorus]
I will trust and not be afraid,
He is my strength, my song;
And when the sky is big and loud
I'll hum the whole night long.

[Verse 2]
Isaiah sang it long ago,
When hard days came along;
He would not let the fear stay big —
He turned it into song.

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
The storm outside can bump and boom,
Heavenly Father's near;
So take a brave and steady breath,
And hum away the fear.

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
The thunder goes. The morning comes.
The sky is rinsed and new;
And every tune you hummed last night —
He hummed along with you.

[Chorus]
mood: Humming music. A small repeating figure that keeps turning under the voice the way a child hums without meaning to — the same few notes coming back, steady, while the weather moves overhead. Fingerpicked nylon guitar holds that turn, and a low string note arrives late in each line like thunder that has already gone past. It begins guarded and close to the microphone and unclenches by the last verse, as though the child has stopped listening for the next crack.
